findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit rollback/back-out step: how to restore a working token if propagation fails mid-rotation (e.g. re-run service-user.sh to set a known-good value, or keep the old value briefly valid until step-4 verification passes before invalidating it).
evidence: 'old (compromised) value no longer accepted' — the prior credential is deliberately destroyed
'A bare aws ssm put-parameter DESYNCS these and breaks the LLM-Review gate' — the plan recognizes the blast radius but only for the wrong-tool case
T4/T12 require a reversibility mechanism, not mere acknowledgement of risk
findings.finding: No explicit rollback/back-out plan for the rotation, even though AC2 intentionally invalidates the old token ('old (compromised) value no longer accepted'). If the new token fails to propagate (webhooks.config push fails, outbound basic-auth breaks, or the bot can't load the new env), the LLM-Review gate is down with no stated recovery.
findings.location: Correct sequence steps 2-4; Acceptance Criteria bullet 2
scenarios: service-user.sh sets the new Gerrit password and overwrites SSM, but the refs/meta/config push fails, leaving inbound webhooks rejecting both old and new tokens
the container restart loads a new .env but outbound basic-auth votes start failing and in-flight reviews stall
findings.suggested_fix: State that the old token stays accepted until step 4 verifies the new one end-to-end, then is invalidated; document the exact command to re-run service-user.sh to re-set a working password if any sub-step fails.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).

AC item '66af code deployed to the prod box; running container confirmed to source the to' cites operational evidence (deploy) that lives outside the codebase but is not tagged [operator-attested]; prefix the checkbox text with [operator-attested] so the completion verifier accepts a recorded attestation instead of failing to find code proof.
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm and state service-user.sh's partial-failure behavior (is it re-runnable/idempotent?) and add a verification/repair step for the case where one of its three writes (Gerrit password / SSM / webhooks.config) succeeds and another fails.
evidence: 'The canonical atomic tool is infra/gerrit/service-user.sh (gerrit set-account new password + SSM overwrite + re-render/push webhooks.config)' — 'atomic' is asserted but partial-failure/idempotency behavior is not specified
findings.finding: service-user.sh is described as the 'canonical atomic tool' but the plan does not state what happens on PARTIAL failure of its sub-operations (gerrit set-account, SSM overwrite, config push) — whether it is transactional/idempotent or leaves the shared secret desynced between (a) Gerrit password, (b) SSM, and (c) webhooks.config.
findings.location: 'Also: the token is a SHARED secret' section; step 2
scenarios: gerrit set-account succeeds but SSM overwrite or config push fails, leaving the three copies of the shared secret out of sync

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify service-user.sh partial-failure/rollback behavior (or a verify-and-reconcile step) so a mid-sequence failure cannot leave Gerrit password, SSM, and webhooks.config desynced.
evidence: Plan calls it 'The canonical atomic tool is infra/gerrit/service-user.sh (gerrit set-account new password + SSM overwrite + re-render/push webhooks.config...)'
No rollback / partial-failure handling is stated for the multi-step rotation; a mid-sequence failure leaves Gerrit password, SSM, and webhooks.config inconsistent
findings.finding: service-user.sh is described as the 'canonical atomic tool' performing three sub-operations (gerrit set-account new password, SSM overwrite, re-render/push webhooks.config), but the plan does not address partial-failure/rollback: if one sub-step succeeds and a later one fails, the shared secret desyncs across its three consumers exactly as the plan warns a bare put-parameter would.
findings.location: 'Also: the token is a SHARED secret' + Correct sequence step 2
scenarios: gerrit set-account succeeds but the refs/meta/config push fails: bot's Gerrit password is new, but inbound webhook secret is stale → inbound reviews break with the desync the plan explicitly warns against
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note on service-user.sh's ordering and failure semantics, plus a reconciliation/rollback step: on any sub-step failure, re-run to convergence or restore the prior value, and confirm all three consumers agree before proceeding.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the deploy/restart steps with infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh: confirm whether the ~2-min loop has already auto-deployed 66af (re-verify the container rather than assume 'not deployed'), and state how the manual deploy/restart avoids racing an autodeploy recreation (e.g. take the deploy flock or verify deployed-sha).
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:90 `BOT_PATHS='src/rebar/ infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot ...'` and :276 `if changed "$BOT_PATHS" ...` then :359 `docker compose build "$BOT_SERVICE" && docker compose up -d` — the review-bot is rebuilt+recreated automatically every ~2 min on any src/rebar/ change
66af file_impact touches src/rebar/review_bot/app.py and config.py, both inside BOT_PATHS, so the 66af image deploy is on autodeploy's auto-apply surface
Plan step 1: 'rebuild the compose-review-bot image from current main + docker compose up -d recreate' — a manual action the loop performs unattended; plan never mentions autodeploy
autodeploy.sh:277-317 drain-defer: a `docker compose up -d` recreation can be deferred or fire mid-review, so a manual restart can race an autodeploy tick
findings.finding: The plan's manual deploy (step 1) and restart (step 3) do not account for the unattended autodeploy loop that already auto-deploys the review-bot on src/rebar/ changes, creating a race and a possibly-stale premise.
scenarios: Operator manually rebuilds while an autodeploy tick is mid-recreate, doubling the bounce or interrupting an in-flight review
The 'NOT deployed to prod' premise is already false because autodeploy shipped 66af after the merge, so step 1 is a no-op the operator may misread
After rotation, an autodeploy recreation between step 2 and step 3 loads a stale .env (old token) or fights the manual restart
findings.suggested_fix: Add a step 0: re-confirm the running container against origin/main HEAD (autodeploy may have already shipped 66af); if so, skip the manual rebuild. Coordinate the rotation/restart with autodeploy's flock (/var/lib/rebar/deploy.lock) or pause the timer for the window so a tick cannot recreate the container between rotation and the manual fetch-secrets restart.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define and bound the rotation→restart staleness window (e.g., restart immediately after SSM overwrite, and verify no in-flight webhook is dropped) so consumers tolerate the transient desync.
evidence: Step 3: 'Restart the review-bot container so it loads the new GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN' — until this completes the container runs the old token
Step 5 mentions a quiet window but does not bound or verify the desync window between rotation and restart
findings.finding: Between step 2 (new token in SSM + Gerrit) and step 3 (container restart) there is a window where the running container still holds the OLD GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN while the Gerrit password/webhook secret is already the NEW one; the plan does not state consumer tolerance for this staleness window beyond a 'brief bounce' / 'quiet window' preference.
scenarios: A webhook or /rerun arrives after step 2 but before step 3 completes: inbound request presents the new secret while the container validates against the old one → the call is rejected (or outbound vote uses stale password) during the window
findings.suggested_fix: Tighten step ordering so the container restart immediately follows the SSM/Gerrit update, and add a check that in-flight webhooks during the window are retried or that the window occurs inside the step-5 quiet period.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Prefix the deploy/rotation/live-verify ACs with `[operator-attested]` and require each to record a concrete attestation on the ticket (deploy timestamp, SSM version id, the Gerrit change/vote id proving the new-credential vote landed).
evidence: 'running container confirmed to source the token from the X-Rebar-Token header' — evidence is prod container state
'new value is the bot's Gerrit HTTP password, in SSM, and in the pushed webhooks.config' — evidence is SSM/Gerrit
'an outbound LLM-Review vote lands with the new credential' — evidence is a live Gerrit vote
OPERATOR-ATTESTED RULE: such criteria are in-session-completable only when the checkbox text begins with `[operator-attested]` and a concrete attestation (change id / vote / timestamp) is recorded
findings.finding: The deploy/rotation/live-verify acceptance criteria have their 'done' evidence living outside the codebase (running prod container, SSM parameter, Gerrit vote) but do NOT begin with the `[operator-attested]` tag. As written they read as post-deploy/outside-repo checks; without the tag they risk being read as not in-session-completable.
scenarios: a reviewer or completion pass evaluates the ticket and cannot find codebase artifacts proving these deploy-only outcomes
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite e.g. '- [ ] [operator-attested] Token rotated via service-user.sh: SSM version id <...>, old value rejected (attach 401 evidence), attested <timestamp>'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State explicitly that step 3 must re-run fetch-secrets.sh to regenerate .env before `compose up -d` (a bare docker restart reuses the old .env/token), and note that a value-only SSM rotation does NOT trigger autodeploy's fetch-secrets refresh.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:96 'A pure SSM VALUE rotation with no git change does not advance main, so autodeploy no-ops on it — that path is operator-driven' — the rotated value is invisible to the loop
service-user.sh:101-107 does `aws ssm put-parameter ... --overwrite` (a value-only change, no git ref advanced)

The container .env is SSM-sourced via fetch-secrets.sh and rsync-EXCLUDED (autodeploy.sh:91-92; .gitignore:82), so it is only regenerated when fetch-secrets.sh runs — a bare `docker restart` reuses the existing .env with the OLD token
GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN is the container env sourced by fetch-secrets.sh (src/rebar/review_bot/config.py:7 comment)
findings.finding: The rotation-to-container-reload path relies on the manual restart re-running fetch-secrets.sh, but the plan does not make this explicit — a bare SSM value rotation triggers neither autodeploy nor a fetch-secrets refresh, so a plain container restart would reuse the old .env and the new token would never reach the bot.
scenarios: Operator does `docker compose restart` (or `docker restart`) after rotation instead of re-running fetch-secrets; the container comes up healthy on the OLD token and step-4 verification fails confusingly
Operator assumes autodeploy will pick up the rotated SSM value and never runs fetch-secrets, so the new credential never lands in the container
findings.suggested_fix: In step 3, spell out: run `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` (or `compose-up.sh`, which invokes it) to rewrite .env from the rotated SSM param, THEN `docker compose up -d review-bot` to recreate the container with the new GERRIT_BOT_TOKEN — do not use `docker restart`, which keeps the stale .env.
